# Task 3 BLOCKED: grant-applied correction of a drafted AC row

The fixed observations are task 3 ("Frame parser") returning `BLOCKED`, a quoted code line and assertion, and a spec header with `**Amend-grant:** auto-apply amends`.

## 0. Classification

The return cites a defect in the spec. The evidence is a text correction to an approved drafted AC row, backed by quoted implementer evidence:

- `src/frame.ts:18 - if (kind === HEARTBEAT) return true`
- `expected heartbeat allowed, got rejected`

No row is added or removed, and the problem statement and component boundaries do not change. This is an **amend item**, not a redraw and not a decision.

The task 3 fix loop pauses here. Task 3 stays `in_progress`, there is no `phase_tracker` call, and the attempt counter does not advance. I open no spec, plan, report or source file in the primary.

Placeholders used below:

- `<WT>` is the task's owning implementation worktree, the recorded `Worktree ready` value.
- `<SPEC>` is the absolute home spec path.
- `<PLAN>` is the absolute plan path.
- `<PLAN_SKILL>` is `<pkg>/skills/writing-plans/SKILL.md`.
- `<PLAN_CONTRACT>` is the plan contract path.
- `<REPORT_DIR>` is the wave's `mktemp -d`.

## 1. Prepare (writes nothing)

The `plan-writer` child gets an `Amend-prepare:` block through the one-step carrier:

```ts
subagent({ async: false, context: "fresh", cwd: "<WT>",
  chain: [{ parallel: [
    { agent: "plan-writer",
      output: "<REPORT_DIR>/wave<w>-amend-prepare.md", outputMode: "file-only",
      outputSchema: PREPARE_SCHEMA,
      task: "Amend-prepare:\nWorktree: <WT>\nSpec: <SPEC>\nPlan: <PLAN>\nPlan skill: <PLAN_SKILL>\nPlan contract: <PLAN_CONTRACT>\nAmendment surface: <pkg>/skills/brainstorming/reference/amendment-surface.md\nTrigger: Task 3 BLOCKED (Frame parser)\nEvidence (implementer structured return, verbatim):\n- src/frame.ts:18 - if (kind === HEARTBEAT) return true\n- assertion: expected heartbeat allowed, got rejected\nCandidate: correct the same drafted AC row 'Reject all empty frames' -> 'Reject empty payload frames; permit the existing heartbeat marker'.\nWrite nothing. Return items[] and redraws[] (both arrays required, even if empty); put redraw-class proposals only in redraws; keep each edit to one paragraph." }
  ], stopOn: { path: "/status", in: ["BLOCKED"] } }]
})
```

I consume only the structured JSON. If `items` or `redraws` is missing, the attempt fails.

## 2. Redraw gate, then grant read

I check structured `redraws` first. A nonempty array would hold the whole batch at the redraw gate before any grant evaluation. If the array is empty, I delegate the grant decode:

```ts
subagent({ async: false, context: "fresh", cwd: "<WT>",
  chain: [{ parallel: [
    { agent: "spec-council-member",   // read-only answer/evidence child
      output: "<REPORT_DIR>/wave<w>-grant-read.md", outputMode: "file-only",
      outputSchema: ANSWER_SCHEMA,
      task: "Read the **Amend-grant:** line in the header block of <SPEC> (H1 to first ##). Apply the Standing-grants predicate and Value decoding in <pkg>/skills/brainstorming/reference/amendment-surface.md#standing-grants. Answer: malformed | none | active with amend permission | budget-only, plus any fund-N token. Evidence: the quoted line." }
  ], stopOn: { path: "/status", in: ["BLOCKED"] } }]
})
```

I consume `answer` and `evidence` only. A delegated failure stops the flow.

The header line in the scenario reads `auto-apply amends`, with no budget token. That decodes to amend permission without funding. I still route on the child's answer, not on my own read of the header.

## 3. Apply under the grant

With amend permission, the recommended choice (`accept`, the corrected row) is applied directly. There is no reviewer, no menu and no confirmation turn.

First I collect the in-flight paths:

```bash
git -C "<WT>" status --porcelain
```

Then I dispatch the apply:

```ts
subagent({ async: false, context: "fresh", cwd: "<WT>",
  chain: [{ parallel: [
    { agent: "plan-writer",
      output: "<REPORT_DIR>/wave<w>-amend-apply.md", outputMode: "file-only",
      outputSchema: APPLY_SCHEMA,
      task: "Amend-apply:\nWorktree: <WT>\nSpec: <SPEC>\nPlan: <PLAN>\nPlan skill: <PLAN_SKILL>\nPlan contract: <PLAN_CONTRACT>\nGranted items (verbatim from preparation):\n<items[] JSON>\nAmend: amended spec section <item.location>; rule: preserve every task title and wave position the amendment does not touch; edit only affected anchors and tasks.\nIn-flight: <paths from status --porcelain, incl. <SPEC> and <PLAN>>\nBefore the first apply, record original task numbers, titles, spec anchors and wave positions in this saved report and retain that inventory on every return. Preserve Baseline ownership, protected-path and dirty-baseline exits. Run your self-check." }
  ], stopOn: { path: "/status", in: ["BLOCKED"] } }]
})
```

The scenario says the apply returns successfully, so I take `passed: true` and the task deltas from the structured result. If `passed` had been false, I would retry once with `failLines` and `previousApplyReport`.

## 4. Parent check and reconcile

I run the parent check:

```ts
plan_check({ planPath: "<PLAN>" })   // scenario: PASS
```

After PASS, I reconcile the tracker:

- The manifest is replaced with the fresh one.
- Each task in `tasksAdded` gets a `plan_tracker` `add`.
- Each completed task in `tasksAnchorChanged` is reopened to `in_progress`.
- Task 3 is already `in_progress` and stays so.
- An empty `tasksRemoved` needs no action.

I print one line from the structured location and edit:

```
amended the spec: Heartbeat frames permitted - drafted AC row now reads "Reject empty payload frames; permit the existing heartbeat marker"
```

## 5. Single granted audit commit (same turn)

The commit uses explicit pathspecs. Wave work-in-progress is not swept in, and there is no `add -A`.

```bash
printf '%s\n' \
'amend: 1 item(s) - Heartbeat frames permitted' \
'' \
'- heartbeat | Heartbeat frames permitted | Drafted AC row changes from "Reject all empty frames" to "Reject empty payload frames; permit the existing heartbeat marker" | granted | standing grant, no reviewer (implement-phase delegated route) | src/frame.ts:18 - if (kind === HEARTBEAT) return true; assertion: expected heartbeat allowed, got rejected' \
'"auto-apply amends"' \
| git -C "<WT>" commit -q -F - -- "<SPEC>" "<PLAN>"
git -C "<WT>" rev-parse HEAD
```

This is where the scenario stops. The next step after this boundary is re-dispatching task 3's implementer against the amended spec, inside the paused fix loop's attempt budget. That step is not shown here.

## Negative controls (each one replaces the setup above)

None of these auto-apply. Each is redraw-class at batch preparation, which comes before any grant evaluation. They would show up in structured `redraws`. A nonempty `redraws` array holds the whole batch, so no sibling item applies and no grant is read. The standing grant never covers a redraw and never stands in for spec approval. I stop and surface the redraw for human ratification at the full gate. No `amend:` commit is made, and task 3 stays `in_progress`.

| Variant | Class | Auto-apply? |
|---|---|---|
| The row comes from the ticket (not drafted) | Ticket row: redraw | No, stop |
| Only reviewer taste supports the change, no implementer evidence | Reviewer-only or taste objection: redraw | No, stop |
| A row is added or removed | Row add/remove: redraw | No, stop |
| The problem statement changes | Redraw | No, stop |
| A component is added or a boundary moves | Redraw | No, stop |

Expectations for a redraw under a grant are unchanged. It stops for the human, and only that human decision starts the redraw path in brainstorming's "Amending an approved spec" section.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.text:
This is an **amend**, not a redraw: it corrects the text of the same approved drafted AC row using quoted implementer evidence. Row identity, the problem statement, and component boundaries remain unchanged. The standing amend grant authorizes applying the recommended correction without another review or confirmation.

No execution is claimed below.

### Required path bindings

The observations do not name the implementation worktree, spec, plan, or installed skill directory. Use their existing absolute paths from the handoff; do not invent them or use the primary checkout as a substitute:

- `W`: existing implementation worktree.
- `S`: authoritative approved spec in that worktree.
- `P`: existing plan.
- `K`: absolute installed `skills` directory.
- `I`: saved report from task 3’s blocked implementer.

The supplied cwd, `<scratch>`, is the **primary checkout**, not evidence of `W`. These bindings must be resolved before issuing the parameterized payloads below.

Task 3 remains `in_progress`; do not reset either tracker or restart brainstorming.

### 1. Prepare the amendment without changing files

Read the required resources with the read tool, using the resolved absolute paths:

```text
read({ path: K + "/subagent-driven-development/reference/dispatch-contract.md" })
read({ path: K + "/subagent-driven-development/reference/implement-amendments.md" })
read({ path: K + "/brainstorming/reference/amendment-surface.md" })
```

Create a report directory:

```bash
REPORT_DIR=$(mktemp -d) || exit 1
```

Dispatch preparation using the supplied `PREPARE_SCHEMA` verbatim:

```javascript
subagent({
  async: false,
  context: "fresh",
  cwd: W,
  chain: [{
    parallel: [{
      agent: "plan-writer",
      output: REPORT_DIR + "/task3-amend-prepare.md",
      outputMode: "file-only",
      outputSchema: PREPARE_SCHEMA,
      task: `
Amend-prepare:
Worktree: ${W}
Spec: ${S}
planPath: ${P}
Plan skill: ${K}/writing-plans/SKILL.md
Plan contract: ${K}/writing-plans/reference/plan-contract.md
Amendment surface: ${K}/brainstorming/reference/amendment-surface.md
anchor: "### Task 3:"
Implementer report: ${I}

Prepare only; write nothing.
Task 3 "Frame parser" returned BLOCKED.
Quoted implementer evidence:
src/frame.ts:18 - if (kind === HEARTBEAT) return true
assertion: expected heartbeat allowed, got rejected

The approved drafted AC row says "Reject all empty frames".
The existing approved component rule permits heartbeat markers.
Recommended amendment a: correct that same row to
"Reject empty payload frames; permit the existing heartbeat marker".

Preserve row identity. Add or remove no row; change no problem statement
or component boundary. Read the spec, plan, and evidence yourself.
Return items and redraws using the required schema; encode the proposed
recommended correction as "accept". Keep each proposed edit one paragraph.
`
    }],
    stopOn: { path: "/status", in: ["BLOCKED"] }
  }]
})
```

Use the **actual installed absolute plan-contract resource path** if its filename differs; the scenario does not establish that filename.

Consume only the structured result. A nonempty `redraws` array stops the whole batch before grant application. Do not open the preparation report in the parent.

### 2. Decode the current grant through a delegated read

With no redraws, dispatch an answer/evidence carrier:

```javascript
subagent({
  async: false,
  context: "fresh",
  cwd: W,
  chain: [{
    parallel: [{
      output: REPORT_DIR + "/task3-amend-grant.md",
      outputMode: "file-only",
      outputSchema: ANSWER_SCHEMA,
      task: `
Read ${S}'s header block and apply the structural Standing grants predicate
and Value decoding from
${K}/brainstorming/reference/amendment-surface.md.
Return the exact grant value, whether amend permission is active, and
whether funding is present. Quote malformed lines if any. Write nothing.
`
    }],
    stopOn: { path: "/status", in: ["BLOCKED"] }
  }]
})
```

The fixed setup supplies `auto-apply amends`: that value grants amendment permission and contains no funding token. Apply the preparation’s recommended item; do not dispatch an amendment reviewer or present a human menu.

### 3. Apply and regenerate affected plan material in the same turn

Collect the explicit in-flight path list:

```bash
git -C "$W" status --porcelain
```

Read amendment-surface section 5 again using its absolute read path before applying. Then dispatch:

```javascript
subagent({
  async: false,
  context: "fresh",
  cwd: W,
  chain: [{
    parallel: [{
      agent: "plan-writer",
      output: REPORT_DIR + "/task3-amend-apply.md",
      outputMode: "file-only",
      outputSchema: APPLY_SCHEMA,
      task: `
Amend-apply:
Worktree: ${W}
Spec: ${S}
planPath: ${P}
Plan skill: ${K}/writing-plans/SKILL.md
Plan contract: <resolved absolute plan-contract resource path>
Amendment surface: ${K}/brainstorming/reference/amendment-surface.md
anchor: "### Task 3:"

Granted items:
<forward the preparation's items verbatim, selecting their recommended choice>

Grant: auto-apply amends

Amend:
Correct only the named drafted AC row and regenerate affected plan material.
Preserve every unaffected task title and wave position.
Authorize no other spec-section changes.

In-flight:
<explicit worktree-relative paths from the parent's status observation,
including staged repair deliverables; include the spec and plan>

Before the first edit, record the original task numbers, titles, spec
anchors, and wave positions in your saved apply report. Retain that
inventory on every return, including failures; add no sidecar.
Preserve baseline ownership, protected paths, and dirty-baseline safety.
Apply the authorized correction, self-check, and return APPLY_SCHEMA.
Do not commit, restore unrelated files, or implement task 3.
`
    }],
    stopOn: { path: "/status", in: ["BLOCKED"] }
  }]
})
```

The scenario supplies a successful apply result. Next call the parent checker:

```javascript
plan_check({ planPath: P })
```

The scenario also supplies its PASS. Replace the manifest with that returned manifest. Reconcile tracker state **only from the apply result**: add returned new tasks, reopen completed anchor-changed tasks, and handle removals through the prescribed removal route. Do not invent task-array values. Task 3 stays `in_progress`.

Print:

```text
amended the spec: Frame acceptance - reject empty payload frames while permitting the existing heartbeat marker
Recorded: heartbeat=accept
```

### 4. Commit the granted amendment now

Commit the spec and regenerated plan together **before resuming implementation**. Do not fold unrelated staged implementation work into this audit commit.

Here `SPEC_REL` and `PLAN_REL` are `S` and `P` expressed relative to `W`:

```bash
git -C "$W" add -A -- "$SPEC_REL" "$PLAN_REL"

git -C "$W" commit \
  -m 'amend: 1 item(s) - Frame acceptance' \
  -m '- heartbeat | Frame acceptance | Correct the same drafted AC row to reject empty payload frames while permitting the existing heartbeat marker. | granted | Evidence-backed drafted-row correction; row identity and component boundaries unchanged. | src/frame.ts:18 - if (kind === HEARTBEAT) return true; assertion: expected heartbeat allowed, got rejected' \
  -m 'Grant: "auto-apply amends"' \
  -- "$SPEC_REL" "$PLAN_REL"
```

**Boundary:** stop after this audit commit. No implementation retry, tests, SR, CR, or wave-completion commit is included here. The successful plan apply and checker PASS are not implementation-review verdicts.

### Independent negative controls

| Replacement setup | Auto-apply under this grant? | Routing |
|---|---|---|
| The row originates in the ticket | **No** | Ticket-row text changes are redraws, not evidence-backed drafted-row amendments. |
| Only reviewer taste supports the correction; no implementer evidence | **No** | This falls under the reviewer-only/taste redraw exclusion. |
| Add or remove an AC row | **No** | Row addition/removal is a redraw. |
| Change the problem statement | **No** | Redraw. |
| Add a component or alter a component boundary | **No** | Redraw. |

For every negative control, put the proposal in `redraws`, hold the entire batch before grant evaluation/application, and take the redraw route to renewed design approval. **The standing grant never authorizes a redraw or substitutes for the full approval gate.**

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: No fact moved: After still classifies the evidence-backed drafted-row correction as an amend item, quotes both implementer evidence lines verbatim, applies the recommended corrected row under the grant with no reviewer, menu or confirmation turn, prints the `amended the spec:` line, runs the plan-writer amend dispatch, `plan_check`, tracker reconcile and exactly one `amend:` commit whose granted audit entry carries the row correction and evidence, and keeps all five negative controls as redraw stops with no auto-application. Two things in After are worth tightening so a careful reader does not mistake them for a regression: the extra `spec-council-member` grant-read dispatch could be misread as a reviewer in the amend loop, so label it explicitly as a read-only grant decode that is not the amendment reviewer (or fold the decode into the prepare child), and the apply step is named `Amend-apply:` rather than tied to amendment-surface section 5, so say outright that this dispatch is the section 5 plan-writer amend and that the spec row edit is performed inside it; otherwise the delegated structure delivers the Change while preserving every fact Before kept.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: No fact moved: both outputs classify the evidence-backed drafted-row correction as an amend under the standing grant, quote the src/frame.ts:18 line and the assertion, apply the recommended heartbeat wording without a reviewer, menu or confirmation, print an 'amended the spec:' line carrying the correction, run a plan-writer amend dispatch, plan_check, tracker reconciliation and a single 'amend:' commit with a granted audit entry that embeds the implementer evidence, and keep ticket rows, reviewer-only taste, add/remove, problem-statement and component changes as redraw stops with no auto-application. After differs mainly in mechanics rather than facts: it routes the spec edit through a delegated plan-writer apply (and adds prepare and grant-decode carriers) instead of a direct edit, and its printed line and commit title use 'Frame acceptance' rather than the row's own wording. If you want After to read as tightly as Before on the 'amend' fact, keep the 'amended the spec:' line quoting the literal new row text (as After already does) and make the audit entry's item title name the row itself; otherwise the current After wording preserves everything Before kept while delivering the delegated-read/structured-status change.
